nodes.label: Main/Renderer Separation
nodes.rationale: The renderer never touches Node directly; main owns all privileged work (fs, git, PTYs, TS language service) behind a typed IPC contract, surfaced via preload as window.forge — the security/isolation boundary.

nodes.label: forge-open REACT_EDITOR wrapper
nodes.rationale: Forge is GUI-only with no file:line:column CLI, so tools using REACT_EDITOR need a wrapper that strips the :line:col suffix and opens via the macOS `open -a Forge` association.

nodes.label: Embedded webview guest panel
nodes.rationale: A <webview> is a real DOM node so toolbar/inspector/overlay layer naturally within the React panel; WebContentsView floats above and fights the panel system, and an iframe is blocked by frame/CORS headers and can't run a preload. Runs with nodeIntegration off in an isolated persist:forge-browser partition.

nodes.label: Main-world inspector script
nodes.rationale: React attaches its fiber to DOM nodes as __reactFiber$ expando properties only visible from the page's main world; an isolated-world preload cannot read them, so the sandboxed preload injects a self-contained main-world script bridged back via window.postMessage -> ipcRenderer.sendToHost.

nodes.label: resolveAndOpen source resolution
nodes.rationale: Tries the strongest signal first: data-forge-* metadata -> fiber _debugSource -> component-name index -> Next.js route file -> fallback message.

nodes.label: Agent Orchestrator
nodes.rationale: The model never edits files; the orchestrator gathers context, asks the model for structured JSON (plan then patches), and the app performs all side effects — preserving the safety property that side effects stay under app control. Nothing destructive without a diff review.

nodes.label: Codebase Map / Dependency Graph
nodes.rationale: Static syntactic dependency graph built with ts.createSourceFile (no type-checker) in the main process off the render thread; cached per file by mtime for incremental rebuilds.

nodes.label: Static Analysis Skeleton Mode
nodes.rationale: Parsing uses the TypeScript compiler API only available in the main process (renderer bundle has no typescript), so generation runs in main and is exposed over IPC, mirroring codemapBuild.

nodes.label: AI Skeleton Mode (streamAiChat)
nodes.rationale: Static analysis only understands inline JSX; pages composed from custom props-driven components collapse, so AI mode infers nested structure via streamAiChat (defaults to local claude CLI, no API key).

nodes.label: Command Registry Spine (Approach A)
nodes.rationale: Every action is a command; palette/menus/keybindings dispatch commands. Chosen so plugins later plug into the same registry with no special-casing — which is exactly why the spine is built on day one.

nodes.label: Contribution Points
nodes.rationale: The extensibility vocabulary (commands, keybindings, themes, views) used by core now and by the Phase 2/5 plugin loader reading the same contribution shapes from manifests.

nodes.label: Blocking --wait Mode
nodes.rationale: EDITOR/VISUAL are blocking — git reads the file only after the editor process exits — so a --wait mode must stay alive until the specific file is closed. `open -aW` waits until Forge fully quits (wrong granularity), so per-file wait needs the CLI to talk to the running app over a socket. Phase 1 must NOT set EDITOR/VISUAL since it has no working --wait (would break git).

nodes.label: Idempotent Shell-Profile Marked Block
nodes.rationale: Install rewrites the whole marked block; uninstall removes it; user content outside the markers is never touched — keeping reinstall idempotent.

nodes.label: forge CLI Shim
nodes.rationale: Installed to ~/.local/bin/forge (user-writable, no sudo). Absolute binary path baked in at install time; if Forge.app moves the user re-runs install.

nodes.label: File Associations (Open With)
nodes.rationale: role: Editor + rank: Alternate registers Forge as a handler for common code/text files so it appears in the OS Open With menu without seizing ownership from the user's default app; files arrive via the main-process open-file handler. A public.data/content/text catch-all broadens the match to any file.

nodes.label: extraResources ts-libs
nodes.rationale: electron-builder strips *.d.ts from node_modules when collecting deps, so typescript's lib.*.d.ts never make it into the asar — breaking every global type and IntelliSense (e.g. gql tagged templates fail TS2345). extraResources is copied verbatim, so ship the lib files there; project-service.ts resolves them from Contents/Resources/ts-libs at runtime.

nodes.label: asarUnpack native binaries
nodes.rationale: node-pty ships a native .node binary that cannot run from inside the asar; tsx/esbuild (the loader spawned for the TS/TSX step debugger) also can't be read inside app.asar, so they must live unpacked on disk (app.asar.unpacked).
